claim_notes: Attribution: Aniskevich Andrey and Bulderberga Olga (2023), Characterisation of mechanical properties of materials used in 3D printing, Zenodo dataset, version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8089569; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8089568. Creator order and spelling follow the Zenodo version record.

Annex 3.1. Characterisation of mechanical properties.xlsx: 1391320 bytes; published MD5 c4842898d2c389ccd7a902691d8a4fa3; independently computed SHA-256 830b2c9277dcc2d03265b63e311a5e7089c258ebb6a389b45d07601ae4b2e4e7.

Only sparse reference-filament measurements and identification cells are curated. Numeric XML lexical values are preserved without changing or recalculating them; source text is organized and summarized into catalog fields. The raw workbook, images, full worksheets and extensive prose are excluded.
The selected measured cells are Tensile modulus E:H: reference filament 2.8 mm, testing at 10 mm/min, MPa. The ISO 527-2-labelled C column is separate and does not establish the measured E:H method.

Samples C27 states that three to five specimens were tested per series and average data were used. Exact row-specific n is unstated. The avedev columns are retained as source-labelled deviations without assuming SD, SE, confidence intervals or a defined calculation.

Zenodo version metadata.license.id and DataCite concept rightsList independently report CC BY 4.0; DataCite HasVersion identifies 10.5281/zenodo.8089569. Attribution, source/version links and license link are retained. Catalog organization and original qualification notes are adaptations; no source endorsement or relicensing under the project MIT license is asserted. Manufacturer evidence has its own rights scope.

provenance.method: Official Zenodo version metadata and DataCite concept metadata checked; one bounded workbook download independently matched the published size and MD5. record.title: Nylon Safety Data Sheet, version 4.002
claim_notes: Manufacturer-authored Ultimaker B.V. Nylon filament SDS hosted by MatterHackers. PDF page 1, sections 1.1-1.3, identifies the product, use and supplier; page 5, section 16, prints version 4.002 and 2019-01-14. These are document revision facts, not study or specimen manufacture dates.

PDF page 1, section 3.1, describes the historical product family as Polyamide (grade based on PA6/PA66); page 3, section 9.1, covers transparent and black product colors. No PA6:PA66 ratio, architecture, blend/copolymer determination, purity, complete formulation or color-specific recipe is established.

This limited historical manufacturer-family fact may support only identity classification for mat_aniskevich_2023_ultimaker_nylon, together with ultimaker_nylon_pricing_20210504 and the separately licensed original study source. Neither 1647 nor M2085 appears in this SDS.

The two historical sources do not establish the studied specimen's lot, manufacture date, exact composition or formula continuity. The study state composition remains unknown; this source cannot support a grade, sample-state composition or measured property. The later generic Polyamide SDS proves neither continuity nor reformulation.
The manufacturer lists both colors, but no black state is admitted from this SDS and color does not create a second identity. No manufacturer numerical property or state condition is imported.
Inspected PDF: 78202 bytes; SHA-256 a25c0275486ca9639fc89ee6a351d29e6e34d0938fa936bf10a9b8e2c42c2863. Original PDF, rendered pages and full extracted text remain external evidence only.

No explicit open reuse license was verified. Only sparse attributed family facts and original qualification notes are proposed. Neither third-party hosting nor the separate Zenodo CC BY 4.0 license grants an asset reuse license; no MIT relicensing or legal-clearance claim is made.

provenance.method: One bounded acquisition through a logged MatterHackers redirect; exact bytes hashed, all-page text checked and PDF pages 1, 3 and 5 visually inspected. Manufacturer authorship is identified within the document; this is historical identity context, not tested-lot composition evidence or independent scientific validation.

record.title: Ultimaker USA, Inc. New York State bidder pricing document, solicitation 23185, Attachment 1
claim_notes: Manufacturer/bidder-authored Ultimaker USA, Inc. submission using a New York State procurement template and hosted by New York State OGS. PDF page 1 identifies the bidder and prints 5/4/2021; PDF creation metadata is dated 2021-05-04. This is a document date, not a study specimen date.

PDF page 3 defines the bidder-stock, item-description and manufacturer-part-number columns; the transparent Nylon row on page 4 lists Ultimaker as manufacturer and 1647 in both part-number columns. This historically corroborates the study's supplier/product-code wording, while no exact study lot or purchase is authenticated.

M2085 occurs inside the product-description field, not the manufacturer-part-number field. It is retained only as a descriptive code, not a verified chemical grade. The description includes an unqualified 750 token; UOM is Each and no package mass is inferred.

This source supports only the product-code correspondence for mat_aniskevich_2023_ultimaker_nylon, jointly with ultimaker_nylon_sds_20190114 and the separately licensed original study source. It provides no composition classification, grade, numerical property, specimen provenance or formula-continuity proof.
No black-product state, color identity split, unrelated product-code correction, price or package quantity is imported. The state composition remains unknown.
Inspected PDF: 233996 bytes; SHA-256 113a0e9157044000a08311bd0d10081ae81fa045197812d41f9393d167d3d1cc. Original PDF, rendered pages and full extracted text remain external evidence only.

No explicit open reuse license was verified. Government hosting does not establish that supplier-authored content is public domain. Only sparse attributed identifier facts and original qualification notes are proposed; the separate Zenodo CC BY 4.0 license is not inherited, and no MIT relicensing or legal-clearance claim is made.

fields.identity_scope: One source-qualified historical Ultimaker Nylon family represented by the Transparent 1647 reference-filament series in Aniskevich and Bulderberga (2023). The manufacturer-authored 2019 SDS describes its Nylon family as polyamide based on PA6/PA66 and covers transparent and black; the manufacturer-authored 2021 pricing submission ties part number 1647 to transparent Nylon. These third-party-hosted historical documents support family classification and product-code correspondence, not the exact studied lot, tested-state composition, manufacture date or formula continuity. Distinction from the existing PA12 representative is based on the documented nominal polymer family, not supplier, SKU, color or measured values. No exact PA6/PA66 ratio, copolymer/blend architecture, constituent functions, additive-free status, purity or universal equivalence of other Nylon products is inferred. M2085 is only a source description token, not a chemical grade. State composition remains unknown.
